agent.problem: Most of the stop's choices depend on discovering unseen wording or details rather than reasoning from the setup. Cards 2 and 3 ask for answers that cannot be inferred from card 1, card 5 asks for an unseen word, and card 6 gives no dependable basis for choosing between shaped and unshaped stones. With four of the five choices working this way, the stop goes beyond the allowed few discovery questions. Add context that supports reasoned picks or replace some questions.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer. A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

agent.problem: The blank asks for the unseen final word of Exodus 20:24. The preceding story card discusses the altar but does not establish the promise, so the baker is guessing the verse's wording rather than reasoning out its meaning.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

agent.problem: Choice cards 3, 5, 6 and 9 refer to the Israelites only as 'them' or 'they,' without identifying the group within the question. Since the preceding story card is no longer on screen, each question needs to identify who God is addressing.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

agent.problem: This non-opening story card has four sentences: the summary, the donkey and eye-for-eye details, the cookie-dough sentence, and 'I looked.' Condense it to no more than two sentences while retaining the long-stretch summary.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

human.problem: This passage is its own lesson, typed Sermons, and almost all of it (Exodus 21:1–23:19) is the stretch the docs name as a long-stretch example. If that rule is applied strictly, Prep shrinks to a few altar cards (20:22–26) plus one summary card. The docs also say speeches, teaching and key laws are not long stretches. They don't say whether that exception covers laws like eye for eye, care for foreigners, widows and orphans, or returning an enemy's ox, when they make up the whole passage.
human.question: When a whole passage is mostly law of the kind the docs call a long stretch (Exodus 21–23), should Prep still sum it up in one story card, leaving a very short lesson? Or do some of these laws count as key laws that get story cards and choice cards? If so, which ones?

human.problem: Card 1 tells events from Exodus 20:18-21, which come before the passage. It marks them with an inline reference, but its verses field cites only Exodus 20:22.
human.question: When an opening card gives context from verses outside the passage, should its verses field include those outside verses, or only the passage verses it tells?

human.problem: Card 8 is the summary card for the long stretch, and it has four sentences. The rules allow 1 to 2 sentences on every story card after the opening. The doc's own good example of a genealogy summary card (Genesis 5) also has four sentences.
human.question: Does the 1 to 2 sentence limit apply to summary story cards for long stretches, or can a summary card run longer, like the Genesis 5 example?

human.problem: This passage is typed as Sermons, and all of it is God's speech. The rules say speeches and teaching are not long stretches. The doc's own example, though, treats Exodus 21–23 as a long stretch, and following it puts Exodus 21:1-23:12 on one card. The stop ends up at 10 cards, and teaching with stated reasons gets no choice cards. That teaching includes care for foreigners "for you yourselves were foreigners in the land of Egypt" (22:21, 23:9), God hearing the widow's and orphan's cry (22:23), "You are to be My holy people" (22:31), and the sabbath year and day (23:10-12).
human.question: In a Sermons passage made of God's laws, should Exodus 21:1-23:12 be summed up as one long stretch, as the doc's example shows? Or should its teaching parts, like the reasons given for care laws and the sabbath, get their own story cards and choice cards?
